answer: Arrival-spacing admission gate. Each new identity must submit eight signed actions over 72 hours, with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a published distribution; a bursty or too-regular stream is rejected. This traffic-shape signal separates organic use from mass registration. Attackers pay one unique active session per identity for three days, plus jitter and bandwidth, so 1,000 sybils need 1,000 concurrent clients and 72 hours of scheduling. A garden of slow clients passes. A canyon of synchronized bursts does not.
